title: 06. Typing & Models: 16. Pydantic (v1 & v2) — Data Validation & Settings
summary: Pydantic is the de-facto Python library for runtime data validation, parsing, and settings, powering FastAPI and many modern frameworks.
objectives: v1 vs v2 — The Cheat Sheet

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: > Pydantic is the de-facto Python library for runtime data validation, parsing, and settings, powering FastAPI and many modern frameworks.

sections.title: 1. Why Pydantic?
sections.body:
| Problem                            | Pydantic answer                   |
| ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| Untrusted JSON / form input        | parse + validate in one step      |
| Type hints not enforced at runtime | `BaseModel` enforces them         |
| Conversion (`"42"` → `42`)         | automatic coercion (configurable) |
| JSON Schema for API docs           | auto-generated                    |
| Settings from env / `.env`         | `BaseSettings`                    |

**v2 (released 2023)** rewrote the core in Rust → 5–50× faster than v1, with API changes.

sections.title: 2. v1 vs v2 — The Cheat Sheet
sections.body:
| Concept                   | v1                                      | v2                               |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- | --------- |
| Field validator           | `@validator("x")`                       | `@field_validator("x")`          |
| Root validator            | `@root_validator`                       | `@model_validator(mode="before"  | "after")` |
| Config                    | inner `class Config:`                   | `model_config = ConfigDict(...)` |
| Parse JSON                | `Model.parse_raw(s)`                    | `Model.model_validate_json(s)`   |
| Parse dict                | `Model.parse_obj(d)`                    | `Model.model_validate(d)`        |
| Dump dict                 | `m.dict()`                              | `m.model_dump()`                 |
| Dump JSON                 | `m.json()`                              | `m.model_dump_json()`            |
| Schema                    | `Model.schema()`                        | `Model.model_json_schema()`      |
| Allow population by alias | `Config.allow_population_by_field_name` | `populate_by_name=True`          |
| Settings                  | `from pydantic import BaseSettings`     | `pip install pydantic-settings`  |

**This guide uses v2** unless noted.

sections.title: 3. BaseModel Basics
sections.body:
```python
from pydantic import BaseModel

class User(BaseModel):
    id: int
    name: str
    age: int = 0
    is_active: bool = True

u = User(id=1, name="Ana", age="30")    # "30" coerced to 30
u.model_dump()        # {'id': 1, 'name': 'Ana', 'age': 30, 'is_active': True}
u.model_dump_json()   # '{"id":1,"name":"Ana",...}'
```

Validation runs on **construction**, **assignment** (if enabled), and `model_validate*`.

```python
User.model_validate({"id": 1, "name": "Ana"})
User.model_validate_json('{"id": 1, "name": "Ana"}')
```

sections.title: 4. Field — Per-Field Configuration
sections.body:
```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

class Product(BaseModel):
    name: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=100)
    price: float = Field(gt=0, description="USD")
    sku: str = Field(pattern=r"^[A-Z]{3}\d{4}$")
    tags: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    secret: str = Field(repr=False)              # excluded from repr
    created: str = Field(alias="createdAt")      # JSON key alias
```

Common constraints: `gt`, `ge`, `lt`, `le`, `min_length`, `max_length`, `pattern`, `multiple_of`, `default`, `default_factory`, `alias`, `validation_alias`, `serialization_alias`, `description`, `examples`, `frozen`, `exclude`, `repr`.

sections.title: 5. Validators

steps.label: 5.1 @field_validator
steps.narration: Modes: mode="after" (default) — runs after type validation; v is already the right type. mode="before" — runs on raw input before coercion. Useful for custom parsing. mode="wrap" — wraps the validator chain (advanced). mode="plain" — replaces type validation entirely.

steps.label: 5.2 @model_validator
steps.narration: Modes: before (gets raw dict) / after (gets the model instance).

sections.title: 6. model_config & ConfigDict
sections.body:
```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict

class M(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(
        str_strip_whitespace=True,
        str_to_lower=False,
        validate_assignment=True,        # re-validate on attribute set
        extra="forbid",                  # 'ignore' | 'allow' | 'forbid'
        frozen=True,                     # immutable after construction
        populate_by_name=True,           # allow both alias and field name
        use_enum_values=True,
        arbitrary_types_allowed=True,
        json_schema_extra={"examples": [...]},
    )
```

`extra`:

- `ignore` (default) — drop unknown fields silently.
- `allow` — keep them as model attributes.
- `forbid` — raise `ValidationError`.

sections.title: 7. Strict vs Lax Mode
sections.body:
By default Pydantic coerces (`"42"` → `42`, `1` → `True`). Strict mode disables coercion:

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

class S(BaseModel):
    x: int = Field(strict=True)     # field-level

class T(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(strict=True)   # model-level
```

Or per-call: `Model.model_validate(data, strict=True)`.

sections.title: 8. Type Coverage
sections.body:
Pydantic understands:

- All `typing` generics: `list[int]`, `dict[str, int]`, `Optional[X]`, `Union[A, B]`, `Literal["a", "b"]`, `Annotated[int, Field(gt=0)]`.
- `Enum`, `IntEnum`, `StrEnum`.
- `datetime`, `date`, `time`, `timedelta` (parses ISO 8601).
- `UUID`, `Decimal`, `Path`, `IPvAnyAddress`, `EmailStr` (extra `pip install pydantic[email]`).
- Nested `BaseModel`.
- `dataclasses.dataclass` and `@pydantic.dataclasses.dataclass`.

```python
from typing import Annotated
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

Positive = Annotated[int, Field(gt=0)]
class Order(BaseModel):
    qty: Positive
```

sections.title: 9. Discriminated (Tagged) Unions
sections.body:
```python
from typing import Annotated, Literal, Union
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

class Cat(BaseModel):
    kind: Literal["cat"] = "cat"
    purr: bool = True

class Dog(BaseModel):
    kind: Literal["dog"] = "dog"
    bark_db: int

Animal = Annotated[Union[Cat, Dog], Field(discriminator="kind")]

class Owner(BaseModel):
    pet: Animal

Owner.model_validate({"pet": {"kind": "dog", "bark_db": 80}})
```

Without the discriminator, Pydantic tries each Union member in order — slower and ambiguous.

sections.title: 10. computed_field
11. Aliases & Serialization
sections.body:
```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

class User(BaseModel):
    user_id: int = Field(alias="userId")
    full_name: str = Field(
        validation_alias="fullName",
        serialization_alias="name",
    )

User.model_validate({"userId": 1, "fullName": "Ana"})
# Dump uses serialization_alias by default? No — only if by_alias=True
u.model_dump(by_alias=True)    # {'userId': 1, 'name': 'Ana'}
```

`AliasChoices`/`AliasPath` (v2) let you accept multiple input names or nested keys.

sections.title: 12. Serialization Options
sections.body:
```python
m.model_dump()                          # plain dict
m.model_dump(exclude={"password"})
m.model_dump(include={"id", "name"})
m.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)        # only fields the user provided
m.model_dump(exclude_defaults=True)
m.model_dump(exclude_none=True)
m.model_dump(by_alias=True)
m.model_dump(mode="json")               # JSON-compatible types (datetime → str)

m.model_dump_json(indent=2)
```

### Custom serializer

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, field_serializer
from datetime import datetime

class Event(BaseModel):
    ts: datetime
    @field_serializer("ts")
    def ser_ts(self, v: datetime) -> str:
        return v.isoformat(timespec="seconds")
```

`@model_serializer` lets you control whole-model output.

sections.title: 13. JSON Schema
sections.body:
```python
import json
print(json.dumps(User.model_json_schema(), indent=2))
```

Used by FastAPI to auto-generate OpenAPI docs.

sections.title: 14. TypeAdapter — Validate Anything
sections.body:
When you don't have a model class but want to validate a type:

```python
from pydantic import TypeAdapter

ints = TypeAdapter(list[int])
ints.validate_python(["1", 2, "3"])     # [1, 2, 3]
ints.validate_json("[1,2,3]")
ints.dump_json([1, 2, 3])               # b'[1,2,3]'
```

Replaces v1's `parse_obj_as`.

sections.title: 15. pydantic-settings — Configuration from Env / Files
sections.body:
```bash
pip install pydantic-settings
```

```python
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict
from pydantic import Field

class Settings(BaseSettings):
    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(
        env_file=".env",
        env_file_encoding="utf-8",
        env_prefix="APP_",
        case_sensitive=False,
        extra="ignore",
    )

    db_url: str = Field(alias="DATABASE_URL")
    debug: bool = False
    timeout: int = 30
```

Sources, in priority order: init kwargs → env vars → `.env` file → secrets dir → defaults.

For nested settings:

```python
class DB(BaseSettings):
    host: str
    port: int = 5432

class Settings(BaseSettings):
    db: DB
    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_nested_delimiter="__")
# APP_DB__HOST=localhost APP_DB__PORT=5432
```

sections.title: 16. Custom Types
17. Error Handling
sections.body:
```python
from pydantic import ValidationError

try:
    User.model_validate({"id": "abc"})
except ValidationError as e:
    print(e.errors())     # list of dicts: loc, msg, type, input
    print(e.json())       # JSON-serialized errors
    print(str(e))         # human-readable
```

Each error dict: `{"type": "int_parsing", "loc": ("id",), "msg": "...", "input": "abc", "url": "..."}`.

sections.title: 18. Performance Tips
sections.body:
- **Reuse models** — class creation is the slow part; instances are cheap.
- **`model_validate_json` is faster** than `json.loads` then `model_validate`, because v2 parses JSON in Rust.
- **Use `TypeAdapter` once and cache** for ad-hoc validation in hot paths.
- **`strict=True`** is faster (skips coercion).
- **Avoid `validate_assignment=True`** on hot paths — re-validates every set.
- For **bulk parsing**, use `TypeAdapter(list[Model]).validate_python(rows)` — single Rust call.

sections.title: 19. Pydantic vs Alternatives
sections.body:
| Tool          | Strengths                          | Weaknesses                                         |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `dataclasses` | stdlib, light                      | no validation, no JSON schema                      |
| `attrs`       | mature, customizable               | no validation by default (need `attrs.validators`) |
| `TypedDict`   | static typing                      | no runtime check                                   |
| Pydantic      | runtime validation, JSON, settings | dependency, learning curve                         |
| `msgspec`     | very fast, schema-strict           | smaller ecosystem                                  |
| `marshmallow` | mature, separates schema/object    | more verbose                                       |

sections.title: 20. Common Pitfalls
sections.body:
| Pitfall                                                           | Cause                           | Fix                                                         |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `True` becomes `1` for int field                                  | bool is subclass of int         | `Field(strict=True)`                                        |
| Mutable default                                                   | `tags: list = []`               | `tags: list = Field(default_factory=list)`                  |
| `validate_assignment=False` (default) skips checks on `m.x = ...` | by design                       | set `validate_assignment=True`                              |
| Forgetting `@classmethod` on validators                           | works in v1, required in v2     | add `@classmethod`                                          |
| Overusing `arbitrary_types_allowed`                               | hides bugs                      | define proper types or schema                               |
| Confusing alias semantics                                         | `alias` ≠ `serialization_alias` | use `validation_alias` and `serialization_alias` separately |
| Heavy models in `__init__` of FastAPI deps                        | rebuilt per request             | construct once, reuse                                       |
